Daily Quiz.question: ১) The duration of 'The Renaissance Period' is-
Daily Quiz.exp:
- The duration of 'The Renaissance Period' is 1500 to 1660.
- It is divided into four main period. Such as-
• Elizabethan Period (1558-1603),
• Jacobean Period (1603-1625),
• Caroline Period (1625-1649) and
• Commonwealth Period (1649-1660).
Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr. M Mofizar Rahman.

Daily Quiz.question: ২) A kind of drama which begins with adversity or discord but ends in happiness is called-
Daily Quiz.exp:
- Comedy is a kind of drama which begins with adversity or discord but ends in happiness.
- Elegy is a Lyric poem mourning for the death of an individual or lamenting over a tragic event.
- Tragedy is a form of drama which presents the fall of a superior human being for a mistake of some kind.
- Ode is an exalted lyric poem that begins with an address to someone, instil anguish in the middle part and ends with consolation.
Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr. M Mofizar Rahman.

Daily Quiz.question: ৩) A 'Blank Verse' is a kind of verse-
Daily Quiz.exp:
- A 'Blank Verse' is a poem with no rhyme at the end but does have iambic pentameter.
- An iambic pentameter line is a verse line of five iambic feet.
- In blank verse, the last word of a line does not rhyme with the last word of any of the successive lines.
Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr. M Mofizar Rahman.

Daily Quiz.question: ৪) A work which has a meaning behind the surface meaning is a/an-
Daily Quiz.exp:
- A work which has a meaning behind the surface meaning is an allegory.
- Allegory হচ্ছে যেখানে রূপক বা প্রতীকাশ্রয়ী কাহিনীর মাধ্যমে কোন কিছুর বর্ণনা করা হয়।
- A Story or picture with two or more different meanings- a literal meaning and one or more symbolic meanings.
- The setting, characters, and things that happen inside an allegory are symbols for ideas and qualities.
Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr. M Mofizar Rahman.

Daily Quiz.question: ৫) Duration of 'The Elizabethan Period' is -
Daily Quiz.exp:
The Renaissance period (1500-1660) is divided into 4 main period.
These are:
• The Elizabethan period (1558-1603),
• The Jacobean period (1603-1625),
• The Caroline period (1625-1649) and
• The Commonwealth period (1649-1660).
Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr. M Mofizar Rahman and Live MCQ Lecture.

Daily Quiz.question: ৬) A figure of speech in which lifeless objects or ideas are given imaginary life known as-
Daily Quiz.exp:
- A figure of speech in which lifeless objects or ideas are given imaginary life known as Personification.
- Examples:
• ''And Joy, whose hand is ever at his lips Bidding adieu''. Here 'Joy' has been imagined as a living person.

Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr. M Mofizar Rahman.

Daily Quiz.question: ৭) Alliteration is the repetition of _____ sound.
Daily Quiz.exp:
- The repetition of a consonant sound especially at the beginning of two or more words or within words.
- Example: Fair is foul, and foul is fair.
- Ruins seize thee, ruthless king!

Daily Quiz.question: ৮) Substitution of an unpleasant or vulgar expression is called-
Daily Quiz.exp:
- Euphemism is a figure of speech which stands for a pleasant way of referring to something unpleasant.
Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr. M Mofizar Rahman.

Daily Quiz.question: ৯) 'The Restoration Period' of English literature started in -
Daily Quiz.exp:
The Neo-classical period is divided into 3 shortened parts.
These are:
1. The Restoration Period (1660-1700),
2. The Augustan Age (1700-1745) and
3. The Age of Sensibility (1745-1798).

Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr. M Mofizar Rahman.

Daily Quiz.question: ১০) What is the meaning of 'Soliloquy'?
Daily Quiz.option4: ঘ) long self speech by an actor
Daily Quiz.exp:
- Soliloquy is a dramatic technique of speaking alone on the stage.
- Example: To be or not to be that is the question. (William Shakespeare, Hamlet)

Daily Quiz.question: ১১) 'There is no one so poor as a wealthy miser.' This is an example of-
Daily Quiz.exp:
- An apparently self-contradictory statement that hides a rational meaning is called paradox.
- Example:
• There is no one so poor as a wealthy miser.
• Sweet are the uses of adversity.
• The world will be saved by failure.
• Ignorance is strength.
• I must be cruel only to be kind.

Daily Quiz.question:
১২) 'The fair breeze blew, the white foam flew,
The furrow followed free' is an example of -
Daily Quiz.exp:
Repetition of consonant sounds at the beginning of words or stressed syllables is known as alliteration.
Example:
“Puffs, powders, patches, Bibles, billet-doux". (Pope: The Rape of the Lock)
Here, ''p'' and ''b'' have been repeated.

Another example:
The fair breeze blew, the white foam flew,
The furrow followed free;
(Coleridge: The Rime of the Ancient Mariner)
Here, "f" and "b" have been repeated.

Source: An ABC of English Literature - Dr M Mofizar Rahman.

Daily Quiz.question: ১৩) Which is the latest period of English literature?
Daily Quiz.exp:
- The Latest Period of English Literature is the Post-Modern period (1939-present).
- The Modern Period (1901-1939) is divided into two shorten period.
• The Edwardian Period (1901-1910) and
• The Georgian Period (1910-1936).
Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr. M Mofizar Rahman.

Daily Quiz.question: ১৪) A poem expressing sadness, especially for somebody who is dead, is known as a/an-
Daily Quiz.exp:
- Elegy is a Lyric poem mourning for the death of an individual or lamenting over a tragic event.
- Tragedy is a form of drama which presents the fall of a superior human being for a mistake of some kind.
- A sonnet is a lyric poem of fourteen iambic pentameter lines.
- Lyric is a short poem expressing personal or subjective thoughts and intense feelings of a single speaker.
- It is identical to a song sung with a lyre.
Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr. M Mofizar Rahman.

Daily Quiz.question: ১৫) 'Ten thousand saw I at a glance' is a figure of speech known as-
Daily Quiz.exp:
- Hyperbole is an exaggerated statement or an extreme overstatement.
- 'Ten thousand saw I at a glance' is a figure of speech known as Hyperbole. (Taken from the poem 'The Daffodils' by William Wordsworth).
Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr. M Mofizar Rahman.

Daily Quiz.question: ১৬) The Victorian Period of English literature is-
Daily Quiz.exp:
- The Victorian Period of English literature is '1832-1900'.
- The Romantic Period of English literature is '1798-1832'.
- The Modern Period of English literature is 1901-1939.
- The Post-Modern Period of English Literature is 1939 to present.
Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr. M Mofizar Rahman.

Daily Quiz.question: ১৭) 'My love is like a red rose' is an example of a-
Daily Quiz.exp:
- A simile is a figure of speech that compares between two different or dissimilar things in an explicit way or directly.
- Example: My love is like a red rose.
- সাধারণত Simile তে দুটি ভিন্ন জাতীয় জিনিসের মাঝে সরাসরি তুলনা বুঝাবে।
- সর্বদাই বাক্যে as, like, as --- as, as like as, resemble ইত্যাদি থাকবে।

Daily Quiz.question: ১৮) An implicit comparison between two different things is called-
Daily Quiz.exp:
- Metaphor is an implicit comparison between two different things.
- Simile is an explicit comparison between two different things. Usually 'as' and 'like' are used in Simile.
Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr. M Mofizar Rahman.

Daily Quiz.question: ১৯) What is a funny poem of five lines called?
Daily Quiz.exp:
- A humorous rhyming poem of five lines is known as limerick.
- Haiku, an unrhymed poetic form consisting of 17 syllables arranged in three lines of 5, 7, and 5 syllables respectively.

Daily Quiz.question: ২০) The 'Puritan Period' belongs to-
Daily Quiz.exp:
Puritanism, a religious reform movement in the late 16th and 17th centuries that sought to “purify” the Church of England of remnants of the Roman Catholic “popery” that the Puritans claimed had been retained after the religious settlement reached early in the reign of Queen Elizabeth I.
Puritans became noted in the 17th century for a spirit of moral and religious earnestness that informed their whole way of life, and they sought through church reform to make their lifestyle the pattern for the whole nation. Their efforts to transform the nation contributed both to civil war in England and to the founding of colonies in America as working models of the Puritan way of life.

King Henry VIII separated the Church of England from the Roman Catholic Church in 1534, and the cause of Protestantism advanced rapidly under Edward VI (reigned 1547–53).

SO, concluding this discussion,
'The Puritan Age' reders the time from 1530s to 1660.
And, The Renaissance Period (1500-1660) of English Literature had also happend that time.
It is divided into four shorter period.
These are:
1. Elizabethan Period (1558-1603),
2. Jacobean Period (1603-1625),
3. Caroline Period (1625-1649) and
4. Commonwealth Period (1649-1660).
So, All these periods also belong to the Puritan Period.

Source: Britannica.com and History.com
